column1: # Known failures of the legibility rules: real faults a rule finds on a subject, each kept here with its issue until it is
# fixed (the harness design, part 2.4). The subject stays as it is drawn; a listed failure does not fail its rule's run.
# KnownFailuresTests.KnownFailuresAreCurrent fails when a listed entry now passes (it is stale), when an entry has no issue
# number, when the number of entries differs from the constant in KnownFailuresTests.cs, so growth shows in that file's
# source as well as here, or when an entry names a rule that has no check in this project yet. This is not R5's allow-list, which will hold looks that are accepted, not faults.
# One line per failure, five cells separated by tabs, none empty: rule (R1, R2, R3 or R5), subject (for a pair of R1 or R2
# "<ink> on <surface>", token keys; for R2's role and resolution checks the key, or "the window's variant"; for R2's
# theme-file check "<file> <key>", such as "hc1.theme GrayText", or "<file>" when the file is missing; for R3
# "<one> and <other>", route kinds; for R5 "<surface>: <part>", as legibility-r5-dark.txt names it), theme case (R1: Light,
# Dark; R2: hc1, hc2, hcblack, hcwhite, fallback, or "contrast" for a check that holds in every set; R3: any of the six;
# R5: Dark), issue ("#" and its number), and one line of why, as each rule's Finding gives them. An entry for R2's
# resolution check covers its set entered from a Light base and from a Dark base alike. An entry for a theme file is judged
# only on Windows, where the theme files are read.
